Lets Windows users eventually benefit from the process-separation project instead of only Unix/macOS users.

categories.name: ipc
why: P2 because it extends platform coverage for the process-separation project's IPC binaries to Windows, which the project has flagged as a goal (tracking issue #28722).
Windows IPC has no real consumers yet (bitcoin-mine/#30437 still open), so the near-term user benefit is limited despite the strategic value.

This unblocks meaningful IPC-on-Windows coverage but only once the underlying feature itself is mergeable.

categories.name: tools
why: P3 because it fixes real bugs in the bitcoin wrapper's Windows exec path (missing .exe extension, wrong error codes, child process never waited on), which would otherwise break the wrapper on Windows.
These fixes only matter once IPC-on-Windows ships; today they have no live consumer.

categories.name: utils
why: P3 because it fixes concrete correctness hazards in SpawnProcess/socket utilities on Windows (a named-pipe hang when a child dies before connecting, a MinGW thread_local use-after-free workaround).
These are confined to Windows-only code paths not yet exercised by any shipped feature, limiting the present-day blast radius.

result.summary: This PR adds Windows support to the multiprocess IPC subsystem so that bitcoin-node, bitcoin-gui, and related tools can build, spawn child processes, and communicate over sockets on Windows. It touches the vendored libmultiprocess subtree directly (with an explicit DO NOT MERGE warning since this bypasses the normal subtree update process), Windows-specific process spawning and socket code in src/util, CI/build/vcpkg/depends configuration for Windows+IPC, and functional test framework changes to support IPC tests on Windows. It is explicitly a draft, based on three still-unmerged upstream libmultiprocess pull requests, and has been iterated on with 31 force-pushes over 16+ months.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's process-separation project (tracking issue #28722) currently only supports IPC/multiprocess features on Unix-like platforms; Windows users cannot use bitcoin-node/bitcoin-gui or the -ipcconnect features. This PR removes that platform gap, addressing libmultiprocess issues #53 and #114 referenced in the description.

open_concerns: PR is based on three unmerged upstream libmultiprocess PRs (#231, #317, #318); until those land upstream, this PR cannot be finalized.
The subtree lint check is disabled with an explicit 'DO NOT MERGE' commit warning because the PR modifies the libmultiprocess subtree directly for testing.
Author has stated other multiprocess PRs (e.g. #30437, #32297) should be merged first to give this PR meaningful test coverage and a real consumer.
resolved_concerns: Sjors's suggestion to combine with #31756/#30437 for easier testing was acknowledged by the author as reasonable but not a blocker.

categories.name: tools
categories.evidence: Substantively changes src/bitcoin.cpp (the bitcoin wrapper) exec logic for Windows path/extension and error handling.
categories.rationale: Fixes real bugs that would break the bitcoin wrapper tool on Windows: '_wspawnvp requires the full filename including ".exe"...' and msvcrt returning EINVAL instead of ENOENT (commit bc7abc5/1bb9ee9). Matters once the wrapper is used on Windows with IPC, which is not yet a shipped default.

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: Substantial changes to src/util/exec.cpp and src/util/fs.h, and heavy Windows-specific additions to util.cpp/util.h in libmultiprocess (SpawnProcess, SocketPair, ExecVp) though most of the latter lives under src/ipc/libmultiprocess rather than src/util proper.
categories.rationale: Fixes concrete safety hazards in process-spawning primitives: a named-pipe connect hang when a child exits early ('If the child exits or crashes before connecting, ConnectNamedPipe blocks forever with no recovery path', commit df65470), and a MinGW thread_local use-after-free causing heap corruption (commit 4e9cf61). These are exactly the kind of subtle, node-wide-risk bugs the utils category flags, but confined to new Windows-only code paths with no current shipped consumer.

uncertainties: Whether this PR should be treated as effectively blocked pending three separate upstream libmultiprocess PRs, or whether those are close enough to landing that a rebase is imminent.
Whether the intentional disabling of the subtree-link lint check (marked DO NOT MERGE) should itself be flagged as a blocking hazard independent of code review readiness.
Extent to which review effort here should wait on #30437/#32297 landing first, per the author's own stated preference, versus reviewing the Windows-porting mechanics in parallel.
Relative weight to give the many small Windows-specific correctness fixes (hangs, error-code mapping) since none have an existing user today.
result.card: This draft PR (open 504 days, 31 force-pushes) ports the multiprocess IPC subsystem to Windows, letting bitcoin-node/bitcoin-gui and -ipcconnect eventually work there, as part of the process-separation project (#28722). It touches the vendored libmultiprocess subtree directly, Windows process-spawning/socket code in src/util, Windows CI/vcpkg/depends wiring, and the functional test framework, fixing real bugs along the way (a named-pipe connect hang, a MinGW use-after-free, wrapper exec bugs) but is explicitly marked 'DO NOT MERGE' because it is based on three still-open upstream libmultiprocess PRs (#231, #317, #318) and needs rebase. Review activity is thin: a single Concept ACK from hebasto in April 2025 and no reviewer engagement since, while the author has kept iterating and has stated other multiprocess PRs (#30437, #32297) should land first. The strongest evidence of importance is that it directly extends the process-separation project's stated platform coverage goal, but there is no current live consumer of IPC-on-Windows, so urgency is moderate rather than critical.
